sections.content: Compare certainty with doubt: *estoy* *seguro* de *que* and sé que normally take the indicative, while doubt or rejection takes the subjunctive.

items.spanish: Estoy seguro de que tiene razón.
items.english: I am sure he/she is right.

items.spanish: No estoy seguro de que tenga razón.
items.english: I am not sure he/she is right.

items.spanish: Sé que algunas ideas son útiles, pero no estoy seguro de que todas sean realistas.
items.english: I know some ideas are useful, but I am not sure that all of them are realistic.

sections.content: A useful shortcut: if you could add 'and that's a fact' to the English sentence, reach for the indicative; if the truth is genuinely in question, as in no *estoy* *seguro* *de* *que*, use the subjunctive instead.
